title: Lesson 11 - MDM styles: registry, consolidation, co-existence, centralized
description: Compare and contrast the various techniques, approaches, and considerations for implementing master data management solutions, including the four MDM implementation styles - registry, consolidation, co-existence, and centralized - and when each is appropriate.

questions.question: An enterprise wants a golden customer view for analytics but cannot change the CRM or ERP to consume corrected data. Which MDM style fits?
questions.explanation: Consolidation builds a consolidated store for analysis without pushing data back; centralized requires consumption change (A), co-existence needs bidirectional write-back (C), and registry provides identity only without full attributes (D).

questions.question: Which TWO statements about the co-existence MDM style are TRUE?
options: The hub both consolidates data and publishes values back to sources
Data is stored only as a cross-reference, never as attributes
It supports bidirectional data flow while sources remain operational
It requires the hub to be the sole author of master data
questions.explanation: Co-existence consolidates and publishes back (A) with bidirectional flow (C); registry-style cross-reference-only describes registry (B) and sole-author describes centralized (D).

questions.question: Arrange these MDM styles from LEAST to MOST invasive to source systems.
questions.explanation: The spectrum runs registry (identity only) -> consolidation (read/report) -> co-existence (bidirectional) -> centralized (hub authors), so B is the correct ordering.
